newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan beheading suspect says attacks were "sacred".
newsitem.headline: Japan beheading suspect says attacks were "sacred".

text.p: A 15-year-old boy held in custody for beheading a playmate and attacking four girls, battering one to death, believed he was carrying out "sacred experiments," Japanese media reported on Saturday.
Quoting police sources, Kyodo News Service said the boy's motives were revealed in a notebook he kept of his actions. He was aged only 14 at the time of all the attacks.
A police spokesman had no comment on the reports but said a notebook in the boy's handwriting was found in his home.
In one entry, dated March 16, and addressed to "Bamoidooki God,", the boy described in four pages how he hit Ayaka Yamashita, 10, with a hammer and then used a knife to stab another girl, aged nine..
The name that the boy gave to his God has no meaning in Japanese and police believe he simply made up the name.
Ayaka died of head injuries a week later, and the other girl was seriously injured with stab wounds to the stomach.
"I asked a girl playing alone in a park where I could wash my hands. She answered I could do so at a school. I asked her to take me there," the boy wrote.
"I said to her, 'Please look back at me, so I may thank you.' When she turned round, I brought a hammer down (on her head). I think I hit her a few times but I was too excited to remember."
The boy's writings revealed that before stabbing the other girl, he chased a small boy to attack him, but gave up when he lost sight of the boy.
In an entry on March 17, the day after his alleged attacks on the two girls, the boy wrote:"I was surprised neither of them have died. I came to know human beings are strong."
In another entry the boy said he was carrying out "sacred experiments to confirm the fragility of human beings,"
A March 23 entry said the boy's mother told him of Ayaka's death.
"There are no signs that I'll be arrested," he wrote.
The boy was arrested on June 28 on suspicion of murdering Jun Hase, 11, whose severed head was found on May 27 in front of the Kobe high school the suspect attended.
Police have said they are also questioning the boy about attacks in February on two girls who suffered minor injuries when they were hit with a hammer.
Media reports have quoted police as saying the boy has confessed to all the crimes.
The boy's name has been withheld because he is a juvenile.
